([[Arden, North Carolina]]) | college = [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (2009–2013) | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_year = | draft_team = | career_start = 2013 | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = *Consensus Second Team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2013 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2013]]) *2x Academic All-American (2012–2013) *[[Pete Newell Big Man Award]] (2013) *First Team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] (2013) *[[McDonald's All-American]] ([[2009 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2009]]) *[[List of NCAA Men's Division I Basketball champions|NCAA champion]] ([[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2010]]) }} {{MedalTableTop}} {{MedalSport | Men’s [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|FIBA Americas U18 Championship]]}} {{MedalSilver| [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|2008 Formosa]] | [[United States national basketball team|Team competition]]}} {{MedalBottom}} '''Mason Alexander Plumlee''' (born March 5, 1990) is a [[forward (basketball)|forward]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball]] team who stands {{convert|6|ft|11|in|cm}} tall.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300170150 |title=Wake Forest Demon Deacons vs. Duke Blue Devils – Recap – January 17, 2010 |publisher=ESPN|date=January 17, 2010 |accessdate=March 28, 2010}}{{cite news|url=http://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/acc/2009-11-12-duke-plumlee_N.htm |title=Duke's Mason Plumlee out indefinitely with broken wrist |publisher=Usatoday.Com |date=November 12, 2009 |accessdate=March 28, 2010}} As a freshman in 2009–10, he was a back-up forward for Duke's [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|national champion]] [[2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2010 team]], which had him playing with his older brother [[Miles Plumlee|Miles]]. He was a 2009 [[McDonald's All-American]] in high school.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncaa/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=4496541|title=Plumlee finding way on the court|accessdate=April 5, 2010|date=September 23, 2009|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Lawlor, Christopher}} During his senior year at Duke, he also played with his younger brother [[Marshall Plumlee|Marshall]]. ==Family== Mason "The White Hawk" Plumlee grew up with brothers [[Miles Plumlee|Miles]], who also played for Duke and currently plays for the [[Indiana Pacers]] of the [[NBA]], current Duke teammate [[Marshall Plumlee|Marshall]], and sister Madeleine.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncaa/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=4496541 |title=Marshall Plumlee, the younger brother of Miles and Mason, is finding his own way on the court – ESPN |publisher=Sports.espn.go.com |date=September 23, 2009 |accessdate=April 5, 2010}}{{cite news|last=Armstrong |first=Kevin |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2010/04/03/sports/ncaabasketball/03duke.html |title=After Detour, Duke’s Plumlee Brothers Arrive at Final Four (dead link)|publisher=NYTimes.com |date= April 2, 2010|accessdate=April 3, 2010}} He and his older brother Miles are the sixth pair of brothers to play at Duke at the same time. Plumlee's parents are Perky, a former [[Tennessee Technological University|Tennessee Tech]] basketball player, and Leslie (née Schultz), a former [[Purdue Boilermakers women's basketball|Purdue basketball]] player.{{cite web|url=http://www.journalgazette.net/article/20100326/SPORTS0303/303269947/1008/SPORTS |title=Duke has brotherhood with Boilers | The Journal Gazette, Fort Wayne, Ind |publisher=Journalgazette.net |date= |accessdate=April 3, 2010}}{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204822517 |title=Plumlees Relish Chance to Play Together – Duke University Blue Devils | Official Athletics Site |publisher=GoDuke.com |date= |accessdate=April 3, 2010}}{{cite web|url=http://www2.newsadvance.com/lna/sports/college/article/duke_prospect_plumlee_a_big_player_with_small_player_skills/5250/ |title=Duke prospect Plumlee a big player with small-player skills | Lynchburg News Advance |publisher=.newsadvance.com |date=May 28, 2008 |accessdate=April 3, 2010}}{{Dead link|date=March 2013|bot=H3llBot}} The two met at a basketball camp during the summer of 1979.{{cite web|url=http://www.jconline.com/article/20100326/SPORTS02010201/3260329 |title=Playing Purdue an emotional matchup for Plumlee family | jconline.com | Journal and Courier |publisher=jconline.com |date=March 26, 2010 |accessdate=April 5, 2010}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010}} His grandfather Albert "Bud" Schultz played basketball at [[Michigan Tech]] (1944), his uncle William Schultz played basketball at [[University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire|Wisconsin-Eau Claire]] (1971–72), and his uncle Chad Schultz played basketball at [[University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh|Wisconsin-Oshkosh]] (1983–86).{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22727&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=1580059&Q_SEASON=2009 |title=Miles Plumlee Bio – Duke University Blue Devils | Official Athletics Site |publisher=GoDuke.com |date=September 1, 1988 |accessdate=April 1, 2010}} "Through the years, I've watched a lot of basketball," said their then-83-year-old grandfather before they played in the 2010 NCAA Championships.{{cite web|url=http://www.postcrescent.com/article/20100331/APC0902/3310302/Neenah-family-has-close-ties-to-Duke-s-Final-Four-basketball-team |title=Neenah family has close ties to Duke's Final Four basketball team | postcrescent.com | Appleton Post-Crescent |publisher=postcrescent.com |date=March 31, 2010 |accessdate=April 5, 2010}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}} ==High school== In high school at Christ School, he helped lead the team to three state championships and a record of 99–8 over his last three years, and he earned a silver medal with the 2008 USA U18 National Team at the [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]].{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204812457 |title=Mason Plumlee Bio – Duke University Blue Devils | Official Athletics Site |publisher=GoDuke.com |date=March 5, 1990 |accessdate=April 3, 2010}} He was named a 2009 [[McDonald’s All-American]] as a senior after he averaged 15.3 points, 10.1 rebounds, 3.3 assists, and 2.5 blocks per game for the year, a Jordan Brand All-American, and a third team [[Parade All-American]] and Slam All-American. He was also named 2009 North Carolina Mr. Basketball by the ''[[Charlotte Observer]]'', and was twice an All-State pick. In addition, he competed in the [[high jump]] in [[track and field]], with an individual best jump of 6’ 8”. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2008}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Mason Plumlee | position = [[Power forward (basketball)|PF]]/[[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = Warsaw, IN | highschool = [[Christ School (North Carolina)|Christ School]] (NC) | feet = 6 | inches = 10.5 | weight = 207.5 | 40 = | commitdate = 2/27/2008 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 4 | espn grade = 98 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2009 | rivals ref title = Duke Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2009 Duke Basketball Commits | espn ref title = ESPN | rivals school = 19 | scout s = 167 | espn schoolid = 150 | scout overall = 6 ([[Power forward (basketball)|PF]]) | rivals overall = 55, 14 (PF) | espn overall = 10, 2 ([[Center (basketball)|C]]) | accessdate = | bball = yes}} ==College== His brother Miles had originally committed to play at [[Stanford University]], but chose to follow him to Duke after Stanford coach [[Trent Johnson]] left for [[Louisiana State University|LSU]]. Mason was elated, as they had been in boarding school together, and never really spent much time apart.{{cite web|url=http://www2.journalnow.com/content/2010/apr/01/sticking-together/ |title=Sticking Together: Plumlee brothers finding their comfort level with Blue Devils |publisher=.journalnow.com |date= |accessdate=April 3, 2010}} He missed the first six games of the 2009–10 season with a broken left wrist.{{cite news|url=http://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/acc/2009-11-12-duke-plumlee_N.htm |title=Duke's Mason Plumlee out indefinitely with broken wrist |publisher=Usatoday.Com |date=November 12, 2009 |accessdate=April 3, 2010}}{{cite web|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/2010/01/07/272691/mason-plumlee-a-key-for-duke.html |title=Mason Plumlee a key for Duke – Duke |publisher=NewsObserver.com |date=January 7, 2010 |accessdate=April 3, 2010}} He and Miles usually rotated into games together, replacing [[Brian Zoubek]] and [[Lance Thomas]], and were often the first two players off the bench. Teammate [[Nolan Smith]] said: "He's an athlete. He can run and jump with the best of them in the country."{{cite web|url=http://www.heraldsun.com/view/full_story/4961988/article-Mason-Plumlee-returns-to-full-workouts-with-Blue-Devils |title=Mason Plumlee returns to full workouts with Blue Devils |publisher=The Herald-Sun |date= |accessdate=April 5, 2010}} Through April 4, 2010, Mason was tied for first on the team in blocks, with 30, and second on the team with 21 dunks.{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204922369 |title=Game Notes: vs. Butler, April 5, 9:21 PM, CBS – Duke University Blue Devils | Official Athletics Site |publisher=GoDuke.com |date= |accessdate=April 5, 2010}} In an average 14.1 minutes of play per game during the 2009–10 season, he averaged 3.1 rebounds and .9 blocks.{{cite web|url=http://goduke.statsgeek.com/basketball-m/players/statlines.php?playerid=2740 |title=The Official On-Line Home Of Duke Statistics |publisher=GoDuke.StatsGeek.com |date= |accessdate=April 3, 2010}} Coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]] said: "Mason has got a chance to be really, really good. He has skills of a guard and the body of a big man, and a great basketball mind. He’s very competitive, he likes the stage, and he’s comfortable with the ball."{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204822517 |title=Plumlees Relish Chance to Play Together – Duke University Blue Devils | Official Athletics Site |publisher=GoDuke.com |date= |accessdate=April 5, 2010}} It is anticipated that in 2010–11 the two brothers will both be in Duke's starting lineup.{{cite web|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/2010/04/02/418963/dukes-kelly-enjoying-the-moment.html |title=Duke's Kelly enjoying the moment – Duke |publisher=NewsObserver.com |date= |accessdate=April 3, 2010}} [[Georgia Tech]] coach [[Paul Hewitt]] views Mason as Duke's best pro prospect.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/tournament/2010/columns/story?columnist=katz_andy&id=5045989 |title=2010 NCAA tournament: A coaching view of the Final Four – ESPN |publisher=Sports.espn.go.com |date=January 1, 2008 |accessdate=April 3, 2010}} Told in early April 2010 that some scouting services view him as the team's best pro prospect, Plumlee said: "I have seen that. I don't even really know what to say to those people. I mean, let's be real. I'm trying to play the best I can, but in reality nobody goes from the bench to the NBA. Come on."{{cite web|url=http://www.news-record.com/content/2010/04/01/article/dukes_smith_always_mindful_of_his_dad |title=Duke's Smith always mindful of his dad : News-Record.com : Greensboro & the Triad's most trusted source for local news and analysis |publisher=News-Record.com |date= |accessdate=April 3, 2010}} Mason has started 11 of the teams 13 games in the 2010–2011 season, 3 of which he recorded double doubles in points and rebounds. For the season, he is averaging 7.5 points, 8 rebounds, and 1.5 blocks per game to help man the paint for the defending champion Blue Devils. He was a 2012–13 first team [[Academic All-America]] selection.{{cite web|url=http://www.cosida.com/news.aspx?id=3973|title=Delaware's Elena Delle Donne, Ohio State's Aaron Craft top Capital One Academic All-America® Division I Basketball Teams|accessdate=2013-02-21|date=2013-02-21|publisher=[[College Sports Information Directors of America]]}} He was also a 2012–13 [[List of Senior CLASS Award men's basketball winners|Senior CLASS Award]] finalist.{{cite web|url=http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/020613aad.html|title=Hulls Named Finalist for Senior CLASS Award|accessdate=2013-02-13|date=2013-02-06|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=IUHoosiers.com}} ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== *[http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204812457 Duke Blue Devils bio] {{2010 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball navbox}} {{2013 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{Pete Newell Big Man Award}} {{Persondata | NAME = Plumlee, Mason | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = American basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = March 5, 1990 | PLACE OF BIRTH = [[Fort Wayne, Indiana]] | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Plumlee, Mason}} [[Category:1990 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players at the 2010 NCAA Men's Division I Final Four]] [[Category:Basketball players from Indiana]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Duke Blue Devils men's basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Parade High School All-Americans (boys' basketball)]] [[Category:People from Fort Wayne, Indiana]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]]
